# 70 PART 2 | Layered Security and Linux

# FIGURE 3-3

```
# grub-conf generated by anaconda
# Note that you do not have to rerun grub after making changes to this file
# NOTICE: You have a /boot partition. This means that
#             all kernel initrd paths are relative to /boot/, eg.
#             root (hd0,0)
#             kernel/vmlinuz-version root=/dev/VolGroup0/LogVol00
#             initrd/initrd-version.img
# /boot=dev/sda
deault=0
timeout=1
hidden
splash image=(hd0,0)/grub/splash.xpm
password --md=$1$yZA5/$G0G7C6BM0eURpMdGSSSky1
title Red Hat Enterprise Linux Server (2.6-18-164.el5)
root (hd0,0)
kernel/vmlinuz-2.6-18-164.el5 root=/dev/VolGroup0/LogVol00
initrd/2.6-18-164.el5.img
password --md=$1$yZA5/$AwR0CIDnMEE6B2a6cP0
root (hd0,0)
kernel/vmlinuz-2.6-18-164.el5 root=/dev/VolGroup0/LogVol00 single
initrd/2.6-18-164.el5.img
"/etc/grub.conf" 23l, 908c written
```

A protected GRUB configuration file.

The password is encrypted with the Message Digest 5 (MD5) algorithm hash. The grub-md5-crypt command is available for that purpose. That command allows a—that is, some random characters to make decryption more difficult. The two encrypted hashes are based on the same password, but appear different because of the salt. One second is left in the timeout to give responsible administrators a chance to open the menu. The password protects access to the GRUB commands, kernel arguments, and GRUB command line.

Note the new stanza, which supports access to single-user mode. While it's protected, there's a risk to have it in the GRUB menu. Nevertheless, it is a feature found in the GRUB menu on Ubuntu systems.

As GRUB relies on a pointer from the MBR, all you need to do is save the configuration file. If GRUB is already the system boot loader, you don't need to reload it. If you're converting from another boot loader, you'll have to install GRUB. For example, to configure GRUB the first SATA drive, you'd run the following command:

+   # grub-install /dev/sda

Yes, these changes make it more difficult for an administrator to say, boot into an older Linux kernel. If that administrator can't access the GRUB menu, he still has the option to use the rescue or recovery mode with the installation CD/DVDs for many Linux distributions.

# Security and GRUB 2.0

Developers are working furiously on GRUB 2.0. It has the potential to be a more secure boot loader than any previous open source system. However, as of this writing, developers have recently implemented the ability to protect options with passwords. GRUB 2.0 has not been implemented in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 5 or the allied Fedora 2 release.
